info.title: ivi-cli
info.description: VISA/IVI instrument CLI with HiSLIP / VXI-11 / SOCKET gateways, scenario-driven mock backend, and Management HTTP/WebSocket API.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: ivi-cli: integrated CLI for managing, diagnosing, and operating VISA/IVI instruments.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: visa
commands.description: VISA transport / SCPI operations.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Register a new device alias.

options.name: --timeout-ms
options.description: Per-device default operation timeout, in milliseconds. [default: 3000]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The device alias to register (for example psu1).

arguments.name: RESOURCE
arguments.description: The VISA resource string (for example TCPIP0::host::inst0::INSTR).

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a registered device alias.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The device alias to remove.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List configured devices.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the human-readable table.

commands.name: use
commands.description: Set the current device target.

options.name: --default
options.description: Also persist the alias as the default device in config.toml.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The device alias to make current.

commands.name: current
commands.description: Show the currently selected device.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON.

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Enumerate VISA resources visible to the registered backends (LXI mDNS + VXI-11 portmapper broadcast, ADR 0008).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON.

options.name: --add
options.description: Auto-register every discovered resource via `visa add` (alias = host portion of the VISA resource). Existing names are skipped.

options.name: --add-timeout-ms
options.description: Per-device default operation timeout for auto-registered entries (default 3000). [default: 3000]

commands.name: query
commands.description: Send a SCPI query and print the response.

arguments.name: NAME_OR_SCPI
arguments.description: Either the device alias or the SCPI text. See examples in --help.

arguments.name: SCPI
arguments.description: The SCPI query when an explicit alias is supplied as the first argument.

commands.name: write
commands.description: Send a SCPI command (no response expected).

arguments.name: NAME_OR_SCPI
arguments.description: Either the device alias or the SCPI text. See examples in --help.

arguments.name: SCPI
arguments.description: The SCPI command when an explicit alias is supplied as the first argument.

commands.name: read
commands.description: Read any pending response from the current (or named) device.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Optional device alias. Defaults to the current device.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show connection state, response time, and IDN for the device.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Optional device alias. Defaults to the current device.

commands.name: script
commands.description: Execute a SCPI script file against the active device.

options.name: --device
options.description: Target device alias (defaults to the session-current device).

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Path to a SCPI script file (see ADR 0027 §2 for directives).

commands.name: monitor
commands.description: Poll a SCPI query at a fixed interval and stream timestamped responses.

options.name: --device
options.description: Target device alias (defaults to the session-current device).

options.name: --interval
options.description: Poll interval in milliseconds (default 1000). [default: 1000]

options.name: --count
options.description: Stop after this many samples (default: run until Ctrl+C).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit one JSON object per sample instead of plain text.

arguments.name: QUERY
arguments.description: SCPI query to repeat (must end with `?`).

commands.name: watch
commands.description: Watch registered devices in a live table, refreshed at a fixed interval.

options.name: --interval
options.description: Poll interval in milliseconds (default 1000). [default: 1000]

options.name: --count
options.description: Stop after this many ticks (default: run until Ctrl+C).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit one NDJSON object per tick instead of a live table.

options.name: --plain
options.description: Emit ANSI-free plain-text snapshots per tick (suitable for CI / log capture).

arguments.name: DEVICES
arguments.description: Device aliases to watch. Omit to watch every registered device.

commands.name: lint
commands.description: Check a SCPI script for unknown command roots without running it.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit findings as a JSON array on stdout instead of plain text.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to the .scpi script to lint.

commands.name: mock
commands.description: Manage mock-device behaviour for the Fake Backend.

commands.name: scenario
commands.description: Manage mock scenarios.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List every scenario.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create an empty scenario.

options.name: --idn
options.description: Optional default *IDN? response for the scenario.

options.name: --initial
options.description: Initial scene name. When set, the scenario starts with that scene (empty, no rules) as its only scene; otherwise the synthetic `default` scene is used.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Scenario name.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a scenario.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Scenario name.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show a scenario's scenes.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Scenario name.

commands.name: activate
commands.description: Make a scenario the active mock.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Scenario name.

commands.name: deactivate
commands.description: Clear any active mock scenario.

commands.name: scene
commands.description: Manage scene states within a scenario.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a new empty scene to a scenario.

arguments.name: SCENARIO
arguments.description: The owning scenario.

arguments.name: SCENE
arguments.description: The new scene's alias.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a scene from a scenario by alias.

arguments.name: SCENARIO
arguments.description: The owning scenario.

arguments.name: SCENE
arguments.description: The scene alias to remove.

commands.name: rule
commands.description: Manage rules within a scenario's scenes.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Append a rule to a scene inside a scenario.

options.name: --in
options.description: Target scene name. Defaults to the scenario's initial scene if omitted.

options.name: --match
options.description: The exact SCPI text the rule reacts to (required).

options.name: --respond
options.description: Textual response (legal for queries).

options.name: --ack
options.description: Acknowledge with no response (legal for writes).

options.name: --fail
options.description: Surface a canned BackendError. Variant tags: transport_timeout, transport_disconnected.

options.name: --fail-detail
options.description: Detail payload for the fail variant (e.g. timeout ms).

options.name: --transition-to
options.description: After the rule fires, make this scene current. Target scene must exist in the scenario.

arguments.name: SCENARIO
arguments.description: The owning scenario.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a rule from a scene by 1-based index.

options.name: --in
options.description: Target scene name. Defaults to the scenario's initial scene if omitted.

arguments.name: SCENARIO
arguments.description: The owning scenario.

arguments.name: INDEX
arguments.description: 1-based rule index inside the target scene.

commands.name: record
commands.description: Replay a script against the active backend and record observed traffic into a scenario.

options.name: --from-script
options.description: Script file whose queries/writes will be captured (ADR 0027 §4).

options.name: --device
options.description: Target device alias (defaults to session-current).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Scenario to record into.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Convert an NDJSON capture into a stored mock scenario (ADR 0033).

options.name: --name
options.description: Scenario name to store the imported scenes under.

options.name: --device
options.description: Device alias filter when the capture covers multiple devices (required in that case).

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite an existing scenario with the same name.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to the NDJSON capture file (IVICLI_CAPTURE output).

commands.name: server
commands.description: Manage gateway servers, routes, and the lifecycle of running listeners.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List configured gateway servers.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Register a new gateway server.

options.name: --type
options.description: Server type: local, socket, hislip, vxi11.

options.name: --bind
options.description: Bind address (default 127.0.0.1). [default: 127.0.0.1]

options.name: --port
options.description: TCP port to listen on (defaults: socket=5025, hislip=4880). [default: 0]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Server alias.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a registered gateway server (cascades routes).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Server alias to remove.

commands.name: route
commands.description: Manage server-to-device routes.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List configured routes.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Bind a public endpoint to a local device.

arguments.name: SERVER
arguments.description: Server alias.

arguments.name: ENDPOINT
arguments.description: Public endpoint (hislip0 / 5025 etc.).

arguments.name: DEVICE
arguments.description: Device alias to bind to this endpoint.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a server-to-device route.

arguments.name: SERVER
arguments.description: Server alias.

arguments.name: ENDPOINT
arguments.description: Public endpoint.

commands.name: start
commands.description: Start a configured gateway server in the foreground (Ctrl+C to stop).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Configured server name to start (see `server list`).

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Send a termination signal to the process recorded in the server's PID file.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Configured server name whose process should be terminated.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Report configured gateway servers and routes.

commands.name: log
commands.description: Tail the structured log file for a gateway server.

options.name: --follow
options.description: Keep reading appended lines until cancelled (default: dump and exit).

options.name: --tail
options.description: Show the last N lines before following (default 50). [default: 50]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Server alias whose log file should be tailed.

commands.name: api
commands.description: Manage the local Management API (HTTP JSON).

commands.name: start
commands.description: Start the Management API listener in the foreground.

options.name: --port
options.description: TCP port to bind on (default 8080 HTTP, 8443 HTTPS).

options.name: --bind
options.description: Listen address (default 127.0.0.1). [default: 127.0.0.1]

options.name: --allow-anonymous
options.description: Allow requests without an API token. Required when binding non-loopback with no tokens configured (ADR 0036).

options.name: --tls
options.description: Serve HTTPS instead of HTTP (ADR 0039).

options.name: --tls-cert
options.description: Path to the server certificate (PFX or PEM).

options.name: --tls-key
options.description: Path to the PEM private key (when --tls-cert is a PEM file).

options.name: --tls-password-env
options.description: Environment variable holding the PFX password.

options.name: --tls-self-signed
options.description: Generate an ephemeral self-signed cert (dev only).

options.name: --tls-client-required
options.description: Require client certificate (mTLS).

options.name: --tls-client-ca
options.description: Path to PEM bundle of trusted client CAs (required with --tls-client-required).

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Stop the running Management API listener.

commands.name: token
commands.description: Manage Management API access tokens (ADR 0036).

commands.name: create
commands.description: Mint a new API token. The raw token is printed once and never recoverable.

options.name: --label
options.description: Human-readable label for the token (max 64 chars).

options.name: --scope
options.description: Capability scope (repeatable). Allowed: read:devices / read:servers / read:scenarios / write:scpi. Omit for a legacy unrestricted token (ADR 0044).

options.name: --expires
options.description: Token expiry: a duration suffix (30d / 12h / 5m), or an ISO-8601 absolute instant. Omit for a token that never expires (ADR 0044).

commands.name: list
commands.description: List stored API tokens (hashes + metadata).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the listing as JSON instead of a table.

commands.name: revoke
commands.description: Remove the token with the supplied id.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: Token id (from `api token list`).

commands.name: diagnose
commands.description: Report runtime, configuration, and backend-registration health.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON.

commands.name: driver
commands.description: Inspect IVI drivers known to the local IVI Configuration Store.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List installed IVI drivers (PRD §6.5).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the human-readable table.

commands.name: logical
commands.description: Inspect IVI logical names known to the local IVI Configuration Store.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List configured IVI logical names (PRD §6.5).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the human-readable table.

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Emit a completion script for bash / zsh / PowerShell. Source it from your shell rc file.

arguments.name: SHELL
arguments.description: Target shell: bash, zsh, or powershell.

commands.name: __complete
commands.description: (internal) Emit completion candidates for the supplied command line.

arguments.name: LINE
arguments.description: The full command line the user has typed (including 'ivicli').
